Careful. One more thing you have to consider is your power supply unit (PSU). What is the power draw in Watts that your PC will need?

For example: 1 hard drive max. use 50 watts + 1 Fan 50 watts + 1 GPU 200 watts + 1 CPU 200 watts; all together your PC will use 500 watts of power at it's maximum performance, so you will want to get a PSU that supplies more than enough power and will last long, so something like a 600 or more Watts PSU from a good manufacturer, allowing for some flexibility in adding extra parts later on.

While your statement is correct, the numbers you quoted are way way off the mark. You don't have to worry about a GPU being compatible with a particular CPU. As long as you have the proper slot on your Mobo you're good.

However, your processor might not be powerful enough for you to take full advantage of a particular GPU's power. It won't keep it from working, but will create performance issues if your CPU is underpowered.

Also, you need to make sure your PSU has enough output to run an external GPU, particularly a high end one.

Short answer, no. You don't have to worry about your GPU being compatible with your CPU, but you're not going to get the most out of your GPU if your CPU can't keep up with it. Also, make sure your PSU is up to snuff to provide enough power for what you have installed.

I foresee two potential issues with an upgraded card in that system. First, the power supply for that base system build is in the 300-350W area, which is quite low. Ocertaxing your power supply leads to overheating, spontaneous hard resets, and damage to sensitive components over time.

Additionally, the ventilation on that case looks to be near non-existent. GPUs can produce a significant amount of heat. If your case isn't suited to venting that heat, it builds up. If it builds up it can lead to more overheating issues, including hard resets and component damage.

Depending on your circumstances, upgrading your PSU and case to more reliable options would be a very wise choice. It would probably run you in the $150-200 range (+ install fees, if required).
